segments.text: What I really mean by conquering my mind is just giving up on the idea that I need external
things to feel fulfilled or happy or like I did something.
And to give you an example, yesterday I came home at about 8 o'clock at night and I was
just terrible.
I had probably one of the worst days I've had in a long time.
And I sat there and I was just thinking like, sure, what do I even do?
I don't feel like doing anything.
I just feel like sitting here and rotting away.
So I decided to take out my journal and I went through and I didn't even write much.
I wrote about a page just talking about why I felt this way, why I felt so upset, so angry
in a sense.
And the conclusion I came to was, I wasn't angry, I wasn't upset, I was just being stupid.
I was just being dumb.
Because when you start to write down your ideas and you start to say them out loud,
you realize how silly you sound.
And I was just having like a bunch of petty, silly excuses to ruin my day, when actually
it was a great day.
I was productive.
I did so many things.
I'm tired, which is such a privilege.
It's such a privilege to expend yourself in a way where you're going to actually make
your life better.
And I came home from that feeling ill, feeling like it was just a wasted day.
And there's something so powerful about realizing how strong the human mind is.
There was this quote that said, the human mind is so strong and its belief is so powerful,
it can believe it's useless.
It can believe that it actually doesn't have a say in anything, that it can't determine
or dictate anything, which is so wrong.
Because really, it's your mind, it's how you think about the world that's going to predict
where you actually go, who you're going to meet.
Because if you're busy operating on this level, how do you expect people to actually get along
with you who are on this level?
You're not going to meet them.
There's a bridge.
And oftentimes, we put ourselves down to this level, we decide what level we're on.
There's this quote in Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill.
It's actually a poem, and it goes along and it's talking about how life lets man choose
his salary, but once it's chosen, it's set.
And it just talks about how every man says, I don't want to ask for too much, I just want
to ask for, well maybe just minimum wage, and life just hands him it.
But those who also ask for a million rand a year, a month, a week, even a day, life
also hands to them.
So really what I'm getting at, the point that I'm saying is it all comes from the mind.
Every action you take is part of something so much bigger than what you really realize.
It's coming from your deep subconscious, something that you're not even aware is actually
working.
And that's what I mean by conquering your mind.
Because just like you, you only see the world through five senses, see, touch, taste, smell,
and hearing.
I might have left a few out.
But you only see the world through those senses, the same way your subconscious only understands
life through your thought.
So if you're keeping your thought negative, your subconscious is just going to be negative.
And what comes out of your subconscious, well pretty much everything.
It kind of just determines, you know, your mood, emotions.
It's the emotion that comes along with the thought.
That's what the subconscious understands and what it can adjust for.
So if you're believing like you're not the kind of person to do difficult things, that's
because you've had the thoughts of, I'm not the person who does difficult things.
And this is where journaling comes in.
This is the thing that's going to help you conquer that.
Because when you journal, when you write something down, it's uncomfortable because it exposes
the level of intellect, the level of depth that you have.
And oftentimes it's so shallow with us.
We give ourselves far too much credit for what we do.
Like when I was writing this here, I was thinking, oh, this is something Nietzsche would write.
But when I re-read it, I was like, dude, this is like toddler level.
And it's in that moment where we realize what we're writing is so silly that we actually
start to think about it and think, oh, okay, maybe I shouldn't have felt that way when
this happened.
Maybe I was just overreacting.
Maybe it wasn't that deep.
And that's when you start really enjoying life, when you start to realize it's not that
deep.
Money is just money.
Happiness is just a feeling.
It's going to come and go.
But if you're searching for it, you're not going to find it.
It's something that's built.
So that's why you have to journal to conquer your mind.
